how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py logic (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed), run through .scratch/fetch_by_page.py because www.ssbwiki.com answers HTTP 403 to the reader's render call, which asks for the page by oldid; the wrapper asks for the same page by title and checks the revision the wiki returns. Every quoted sentence below was checked, by script, to appear word for word in the page text read at the revision named. SmashWiki pages cover every Smash game; a line states a Melee fact only where the page says so for Melee (the 'In Super Smash Bros. Melee' trophy text, a sentence naming Melee, or a Melee table column), or describes the item or enemy for the whole series without naming a game.

lines.line: Summary: A close-range item from the Donkey Kong arcade game. Whoever grabs it swings nonstop, and its knockback is extremely strong and vertical.

quoted: The Hammer (ハンマー, Hammer) is a close-range item that appears in all Super Smash Bros. games.
The hammer comes from the arcade game Donkey Kong.
they will constantly swing the hammer back and forth
it also deals extremely high vertical knockback

lines.line: Uses: Swings do heavy damage and knockback. Holders cannot guard, use specials or jump again in the air, so a ledge knock-off can KO them.

quoted: Upon being grabbed by any player, it sends them into a unique state that inflicts significant damage and knockback.
they will constantly swing the hammer back and forth, and will be unable to midair jump, use any other attacks, or defend
As the wielder of the hammer cannot use special moves or midair jump, sending an opponent off a ledge while they swing the Hammer can effectively KO them unless they can somehow drop the Hammer.

lines.line: Tips: From Melee on, one pickup in eight loses the head. Once it falls off, the head makes a strong throwing item.

quoted: Starting in Melee, there is a 12.5% chance (one out of eight) of the head of the Hammer falling off as it is picked up, after which the item becomes functionally useless, though the wielder will continue to swing the handle for as long as they would with a normal hammer.
The Hammer Head itself can be picked up and thrown as a powerful item.

lines.line: Summary: A battering item with long reach, nicknamed the lightsaber because it looks like one. Holding it adds power, and you can charge it or throw it.

quoted: The Beam Sword (ビームソード, Beam Sword) is a long-range battering item.
It is similar in appearance to a lightsaber, and is often informally referred to as the "lightsaber" for this reason.
it can be wielded and charged for melee attacks or can be thrown, like all other battering items.
the Beam Sword will bolster the player's power, as well as potentially add some options to their game via throwing.

lines.line: Tips: Its reach grows most on charged smashes in Melee. Peach can pull one out with Vegetable, but the Melee odds are 1/768.

quoted: In Melee and Brawl, the Beam Sword's range significantly increases in size, particularly in the case of charged smash attacks.
In Melee and Brawl, a Beam Sword is one of few unusual items Peach can pull out via her Vegetable attack, though the chances of this are slim; 1/768 and 1/480 in Melee and Brawl respectively.

lines.line: Summary: An odd mix of battering item and projectile item, loaded with sixteen stars. Thrown, it hits with strong semi-spike knockback.

quoted: the Star Rod acts as an unusual combination of both battering and projectile items.
The item, however, has only sixteen stars, and using either of the two aforementioned characters can cause the item to quickly deplete its ammunition.

A more practical option, however, is to throw the item towards enemies; the Star Rod, when thrown, deals powerful semi-spike knockback, which can potentially gimp recoveries or act as a general KO move.

lines.line: Uses: Swing it for close hits, or use a smash or tilt to fire stars. Falcon's forward smash fires 5 stars at once and Sheik's fires 2.

quoted: As a battering item, combatants can use the Star Rod to directly hit opponents up close.
Using either smash attacks or tilts, however, cause the Star Rod to shoot out long-range stars that can hit opponents from a distance
with Falcon's attacks shooting off 5 stars and Sheik's firing off 2 stars.
Particularly powerful variants are found with the forward smashes of Captain Falcon, Marth, Sheik, Pit and Ike

lines.line: Tips: Once empty, throwing it is the more practical choice: the semi-spike can ruin a recovery or act as a KO. Reflecting or absorbing moves can stop its stars.

quoted: A more practical option, however, is to throw the item towards enemies; the Star Rod, when thrown, deals powerful semi-spike knockback, which can potentially gimp recoveries or act as a general KO move.
As the stars are considered projectiles by the game, they can be reflected by a variety of moves; in addition, they can also be absorbed.
If the Star Rod runs out of stars to shoot, combatants can still use it to directly hit opponents.

lines.line: Summary: A long-range shooting item modelled on an actual Nintendo accessory. In Melee a tap fires three small shots, and holding the button charges a bigger one.

quoted: is a shooting item that appears in Super Smash Bros. Melee, Super Smash Bros. Brawl, Super Smash Bros. 4, and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, based on a real-life peripheral from Nintendo.
Tapping the attack button will fire three small shots in Melee
Holding down the attack button charges the weapon, allowing for stronger and larger shots and having decent KO potential at full charge.

lines.line: Uses: Mash the button for a stream of weak shots that leave foes almost no time to act. A bigger charge costs more of Melee's 48 shots.

quoted: If the player constantly taps the attack button, they will fire a constant stream of small shots, each of which does little knockback and damage.
The high rate of fire and low knockback causes a "trapping" effect as the opponent will have little-to-no time to act
The Super Scope has limited ammunition, with 48 shots in Melee and Brawl
Different charge levels will increase the ammo used.

lines.line: Tips: Uncharged shots pass through foes, so one burst can trap several. Their 280 degree angle makes a weak meteor smash, and an empty Scope only puffs smoke.

quoted: In Melee, the uncharged shots have a 280° knockback angle, resulting in a very weak meteor smash, making it ineffective against opponents close to the stage.
The uncharged shots can also pass through opponents, allowing it to trap multiple enemies
Attempting to use the Super Scope after it runs out of ammunition causes it to fire nothing but a puff of smoke

lines.line: Summary: A long-range weapon whose sideways knockback makes it easy to juggle foes at low percents.

quoted: The Ray Gun (レイガン, Ray Gun) is a long-range weapon used in all games of the Super Smash Bros. series.
The horizontal knockback allows it to easily juggle opponents at low percents

lines.line: Uses: It holds 16 shots, each doing 4% in Melee, and can fire once every 30 frames. At middle percents the sideways push carries foes to the blast line.

quoted: A Ray Gun can be shot 16 times before it runs out of ammunition.
In Super Smash Bros. Melee, Super Smash Bros. Brawl, and Super Smash Bros. 4 each shot deals 4% without electricity, horizontal knockback, and can be fired every 30 frames.
The horizontal knockback allows it to easily juggle opponents at low percents or to carry them to the blast line at mid percents.

lines.line: Tips: A reflector can send back both the shots and a thrown gun, while an absorber only works on the shots.

quoted: The shots can be reflected or absorbed, while the gun itself (when thrown) can only be reflected.

lines.line: Summary: Two items that heal: either one lowers the damage percentage of whoever grabs it. In Melee a Maxim Tomato takes 50% off, and a Heart Container takes off 100% in total.

quoted: is a healing item (a red tomato with a black "M" in the center) first introduced in the Kirby series, which reduces the damage percentage of the player who picks it up.
Beginning in Super Smash Bros. Melee, the Maxim Tomato heals 50% from a character's damage percentage, with Heart Containers taking the previous function of healing 100% damage.
is an item that will reduce the damage of the character who picks it up.
Heart Containers function similarly to 64. However, it now only heals a total of 100%.

lines.line: Uses: Damage you take while a Maxim Tomato heals comes off what it restores, so a 10% hit leaves only 40% healed.

quoted: Also beginning in Melee, damage taken while healing will be subtracted from the amount healed by the tomato.
if an attack does 10% damage, the tomato will "absorb" it into its 50% recovery, and the user only recovers 40% damage.

lines.line: Looks like: A little red tomato with an M, in black and white, on its front.

quoted: The Maxim Tomato is a small red tomato, with a noticeable black and white M on the front.

lines.line: Tips: The All-Star Rest Area hands you three Heart Containers, and these heal every point of your damage, not just 100%. A glitch in Melee cuts a Heart Container's healing short if you step into the teleporter, so you are not fully healed.

quoted: The player is given three Heart Containers in the All-Star Rest Area that can heal all of their damage instead of the standard 100%.
Due to a glitch, entering the teleporter in Melee will interrupt the Heart Container's healing and thus not fully heal the player.

lines.line: Summary: First seen in Melee, this item makes whoever smashes it become a Metal fighter for a short while. Metal fighters are far heavier and walk more slowly, but fall faster.

quoted: The Metal Box item debuted as a transforming item in Super Smash Bros. Melee.
The Metal Box transforms the player's fighter who breaks it into a Metal fighter.
The effects last 12 seconds
Increases the fighter's weight (3.0× in Melee
Decreases the fighter's walking speed slightly (0.7× in Melee
Increases the fighter's falling speed (2.0× in Melee and Brawl

lines.line: Uses: The effect lasts 12 seconds in Melee, but damage shortens it, fire attacks most of all. Your walking speed is multiplied by 0.7 and your jump force by 1.55, which is usually not enough to offset how fast you fall.

quoted: The effects last 12 seconds, but the time limit decreases as the fighter takes damage, especially from fire attacks like Bowser's Fire Breath.
Decreases the fighter's walking speed slightly (0.7× in Melee, Brawl, and Smash 4; 0.8× in Ultimate).
Increases the fighter's jump force (1.55× in Melee and Brawl;
although usually not by enough to compensate for the gravity and fall speed increase

lines.line: Tips: Falling faster makes it harder to get back to the stage. In Melee a Metal Box vanishes if a projectile touches it, but disjointed attacks, and any hit from a character wielding a sword, still break it and still make the attacker metal.

quoted: making recoveries harder and more vulnerable to certain chain grabs.
In Melee, if the Metal Box is broken by disjointed attacks like Pikachu's forward smash or any attack from a sword-wielding character, they will still transform them into a Metal fighter.
Also, if the Metal Box is hit by a projectile, it will disappear.

lines.line: Summary: A Mario item, called the Starman in Melee, that gives you ten seconds of invincibility.

quoted: The Super Star (スーパースター, Super Star), known as the Starman prior to the PAL release of Super Smash Bros. Brawl and the NTSC release of Super Smash Bros. 4, is an item from the Mario series.
The player's fighter will become invincible for ten seconds

lines.line: Uses: Melee copies the first game here: running into foes does not damage them.

quoted: The Starman returns as an item, reprising its behavior from Super Smash Bros.
The player's fighter will become invincible for ten seconds, but it doesn't damage the opponents when touched.

lines.line: Looks like: The fighter who takes it sparkles brightly.

quoted: Also, the player's fighter will be given a bright, sparkling appearance

lines.line: Tips: It ricochets in big arcs over the field, off platforms and walls, and it can fall off the stage if nobody grabs it in time. In Melee, the star's own tune pushes the stage music down until you can barely hear it.

quoted: The Super Star bounces on the field and off platforms or walls in large arcs, and can fall off the stage if not grabbed in time
Unlike in the previous game, the Starman's theme music lowers the stage music's volume to the point that it becomes extremely difficult to hear

lines.line: Summary: Two Mario items that change your size for about ten seconds. The Super Mushroom, new in Melee, makes you bigger, and the Poison Mushroom shrinks you.

quoted: The Super Mushroom debuts as a transformation item, with the effects described above.
The transformation lasts about ten seconds.
The Poison Mushroom debuted as an effect item in Super Smash Bros. Melee.
The player's fighter will shrink smaller after touching it
The transformation lasts about ten seconds.

lines.line: Uses: In Melee a Super Mushroom multiplies your weight by 1.6 and direct-attack damage by 1.2, but gives no armor. A Poison Mushroom does the reverse, shrinking you and cutting weight and attack damage.

quoted: Increases the fighter's weight (applies a 1.6× multiplier in Melee
Increases the base power of direct attacks (1.2× in Melee
The item does not offer any armor, however, so the fighter will still flinch from attacks that deal any amount of knockback.
The player's fighter will shrink smaller after touching it
Decreases the player's fighter's weight by a small amount
Decreases the damage dealt by direct attacks

lines.line: Looks like: You can tell the Poison Mushroom from a Super Mushroom by its angry eyes and duller colours.

quoted: They are mushrooms that deceptively resemble the Super Mushroom, but with a duller color scheme and angry eyes.

lines.line: Tips: Both mushrooms drift rightward after they appear, though in Melee one that appears on the stage's right side drifts left instead. If you touch one while the other is working on you, you go back to normal size. In Melee, if you jump just as a Super Mushroom runs out, you get a super jump about the height of two jumps taken in a Bunny Hood.

quoted: The Super Mushroom appears on the stage and keeps sliding to the right. In Super Smash Bros. Melee, it will slide left if it spawns on the right half of the stage.
Touching a Super Mushroom while under the effect of a Poison Mushroom and vice versa will restore a character to their normal size
In Melee, jumping at the moment that the Super Mushroom's effects wear off also causes characters to perform a super jump that is almost as high as two jumps while wearing the Bunny Hood.
It will appear on the stage and keeps sliding to the right. In Melee, it will slide left if it spawns on the right half of the stage.

lines.line: Summary: Enemies you meet often in Melee's single-player modes, with male and female versions. They are mostly weak, light fighters who go down very easily.

quoted: are common enemies in various 1-player modes in Super Smash Bros. Melee.
Fighting Wire Frames come in male and female varieties
Generally, they are weak and light fighters, and are very easy to KO

lines.line: Weak points: They cannot charge smash attacks, and with no special moves they rely on high jumps to get back. Their attacks are much weaker copies of Captain Falcon's and Zelda's.

quoted: as to compensate their lack of recoveries due to their inability to use special moves, the Fighting Wire Frames have high jumping prowess.
They are also unable to charge smash attacks and their moves are much weaker versions of Captain Falcon and Zelda's attacks.

lines.line: Looks like: Pink lines forming the outline of a person. The face bears the logo of Super Smash Bros. and the chest holds something red shaped like a heart. They are bigger than the fighters they copy.

quoted: are, true to their name, a framework of pink lines in a humanoid shape
Their faces feature the Super Smash Bros. logo, and a red heart-like object can be found within their chests.
The Fighting Wire Frames are also larger than their counterparts

lines.line: Tips: Males always chase after your character, while females hang back and seldom go straight for you. In Cruel Melee every one of them is fiercely aggressive, hits very hard and is tougher to knock off the stage, so surviving among them is hard. In Adventure Mode you fight them on a Battlefield with low gravity, and there and in Multi-Man Melee neither Star KOs nor Screen KOs work on them.

quoted: males always home towards the player's character, whereas the females tend to play a more passive role, rarely directly assaulting or attacking the player.
In Cruel Melee, however, all Wire Frames are extremely aggressive, and are also handicapped to be extremely powerful and harder to knock off-stage.
Characters cannot survive easily among the Wire Frames because of their amplified power and aggressive edge-guarding.
In Adventure Mode, the Fighting Wire Frames are fought in a low-gravity version of Battlefield.
In Adventure Mode and Multi-Man Melee, the Wire Frames have the property of being unable to be Star or Screen KO'd

lines.line: Summary: The closing fight of Classic Mode, set on Melee's Final Destination. You win by draining a fixed amount of HP, and in Melee how much depends on the difficulty.

quoted: He is the final boss of the 1-player Classic Mode, and has a set HP which must be depleted to win
He is fought on the Melee version of Final Destination.
His HP is now dependent on difficulty, instead of having 300 HP regardless of difficulty.

lines.line: Weak points: In Melee this boss can no longer turn around. Where it moves is set wholly by the attack it is performing and where you stand, and between attacks it goes back to where it started.

quoted: he loses the ability to turn around
Master Hand's movement is now entirely dependent on the attack he's using and the player's position; he always returns to his starting position when not attacking.

lines.line: Looks like: A glove. In Melee the wrist just fades out instead of ending at a cuff.

quoted: instead of appearing as a glove with a "cuff", Master Hand's "wrist" fades into nothingness.

lines.line: Tips: It gets stronger at each difficulty step, and the top levels give it a lot of attacks that can finish you in one hit. A laser leaves each of its fingertips. When it makes a gun shape, it fires one pair of bullets until it has taken 150% damage, and three pairs after that. Its ground slap buries a player; its ground throw cannot normally KO, though it deals big damage and knockback. On Normal or harder, if you take off half its HP within 5 minutes 50 seconds of Classic Mode starting, a second boss joins the fight.

quoted: In addition to this increase in HP, his power increases with each increment in difficulty, with the highest levels giving him a multitude of attacks with OHKO potential.
Master Hand shoots a laser beam from each of his fingertips.
Master Hand makes the shape of a gun, and fires pairs of bullets.
He fires one pair if he hasn't taken 150% damage yet, and three pairs if he took 150% damage or more.
Master Hand slaps the ground. Buries the player.
Master Hand throws the opponent into the ground.
High damage and knockback, but cannot KO under normal conditions.
to fight him, one must play Classic Mode on Normal difficulty or higher, reach Master Hand, and reduce Master Hand's HP by half within a total of 5 minutes and 50 seconds since the start of the mode.

sections.name: A hidden boss in Classic Mode

lines.line: Summary: A bonus boss that can join Classic Mode's last fight alongside the final boss, but only when the conditions the game sets for it are met.

quoted: In Classic Mode, he appears as a bonus boss fought alongside Master Hand
Crazy Hand appears when set conditions are met.

lines.line: Weak points: Its HP at the start is the same as the first boss's. When it lies on the floor and thrashes, that attack cannot reach anyone in the air, and any bomb it drops that hits a character before landing deals little damage and almost no knockback.

quoted: Crazy Hand starts with the same number of HP that Master Hand started with (dependent on the difficulty).
Crazy Hand lies on the ground and has violent spasms.
Very large hitbox and sends opponents upward, but cannot hit aerial targets.
Crazy Hand drops several bombs.
If a bomb hits a character before it hits the ground, it does low damage with minimal knockback.

lines.line: Looks like: It looks just like the final boss, except that it is a left hand.

quoted: Crazy Hand's basic appearance is exactly the same as Master Hand's (apart from being a left hand)

lines.line: Tips: Most of its moves are beefed-up versions of the final boss's, with a few that are its own. The fist it flies in with from behind the stage can star KO from as little as 35%, its forward throw can KO at low damage if you do not use DI, and the last of its three pokes can star KO at mid to high percentages.

quoted: Most of Crazy Hand's attacks are stronger variations of Master Hand's; however he also has a few unique attacks of his own.
Crazy Hand flies in from behind the stage as a fist, causing an electrical explosion on crossing the playing field.
star KOing as low as 35%.
Crazy Hand throws the opponent forward with very high horizontal knockback, KOing the player at low percentages without DI.
Crazy Hand pokes three times.
being capable of star KOing any players at middle to high percentage.

lines.line: Summary: Every so often a quake shakes Brinstar and acid begins to climb, at times submerging part of the stage. It does damage and medium knockback, and it takes a very high percent before it can KO, although in Melee a glitch with the ceiling lets it KO at extremely low percents.

quoted: Occasionally, an earthquake occurs and, just like Planet Zebes, acid starts to rise, sometimes covering parts of the stage.
The acid deals damage and moderate knockback, but will not KO until very high percents
in Melee, the ceiling glitch can cause players to be unfairly K.Oed at extremely low percents by the acid

lines.line: Looks like: Yellow acid, with a large pool of it in the background under a brain-like creature.

quoted: Direct references to Brinstar include the yellow acid
The background is occupied by a large pool of acid with an unidentified life form hanging above it.

lines.line: Tips: While it climbs, it generally stops anyone being KO'd off the lowest blast line. It climbs and halts at irregular spacing, seldom reaches its peak, where everything but the highest platform is covered, and after a while it drains away. Grabbing the Super Star lets a character avoid it. Attacks can wear down the fleshy parts that hold the stage together, and while they regrow you can drop through them. In Melee, touching the acid makes a distinctive splash and a sizzling sound.

quoted: While it is rising it will generally prevent characters from being KO'd on the bottom blast line.
It will rise and pause at various intervals, rarely reaching its highest point where it will cover everything except the topmost platform
After a while, the acid subsides.
said blob can be weakened by attacks, and when destroyed the main platform gets separated.
While regenerating, the substance that holds the stage together is fall-through.
In Melee, when a fighter makes contact with the acid, a unique splash effect erupts from the acid with a distinct sizzling sound.
Characters who have grabbed the Super Star can avoid the acid in Planet Zebes and Brinstar

lines.line: Summary: Thirty F-Zero Racers act as a hazard on Mute City. They keep driving around the track, though they appear only on some stretches of it, and only at certain times and on certain laps. Touching one hurts and sends you upward.

quoted: The thirty F-Zero Racers are another level hazard.
They drive around the track continuously (though they only appear on certain segments of the track, and at alternating times and laps) and will damage any player upon contact, sending them upwards.

lines.line: Weak points: Racers can be hurt, and even blown up, by explosives like the Motion-Sensor Bomb, by strong attacks, by items such as the Home-Run Bat and the Hammer, and by stationary Pokémon such as Venusaur or Charizard.

quoted: However, the racers can be damaged and even destroyed by hitting them with explosives (such as the Motion-Sensor Bomb), powerful attacks and items (like the Hammer and Home-Run Bat) and immovable Pokémon (like Venusaur or Charizard).

lines.line: Tips: A racer that is destroyed leaves its wreck lying where it blew up until the match ends. If the platform is floating above the track and you touch the track, you take damage too. On Adventure Mode's F-Zero stage, a large "!" appears on screen as cars approach, each hit costs 35%, and pink platforms along the track can be hopped onto to stay clear.

quoted: when enough damage is dealt to them by fighters or explosives laid on the track, they will explode and the wreckage will stay at that same point for the rest of the match.
If a player makes contact with the track while the platform is hovering, they will be damaged
A giant "!" on the screen indicates that race cars are approaching. If a car hits the player, then they will take 35% damage.
The player can jump on pink platforms that are situated throughout the stage to avoid being hit by the cars

lines.line: Summary: At irregular intervals the stage turns into one of four variants picked at random, each themed on a Pokémon type, then goes back to normal and starts over. The same variant can come up two times running.

quoted: After a varying period of time, the basic stage transforms into a random one of four variants, each based on a type from the Pokémon series.
After a while, the stage reverts to the basic form, and the cycle repeats. The same variant can occur consecutively.

lines.line: Looks like: The normal stage is symmetrical: one big main platform with two soft platforms hovering over it. Behind it you see a huge jumbotron, a crowd and fireworks.

quoted: The basic stage is symmetrical and consists of one large main platform, with two floating soft platforms above.
In the background, a large crowd watches the fight while fireworks go off in the sky. There is a large jumbotron

lines.line: Tips: The big screen shows a symbol of the coming variant while the stage is changing. In Melee tournaments, many players wait through the Fire and Rock forms by staying on the far side of the stage from their opponent until it returns to normal, and many say this wastes time. On the Fire variant in Melee, a character hit toward the right of the tree's base may fall through. The flames behind the Fire variant are decoration only. On the Water variant's windmill, whoever stands on the lowest arm falls, and in Melee its arms are soft.

quoted: Note that the fire in the background is purely aesthetic and has no gameplay effect.
Its arms spin slowly and can be stood upon, but players on the current lowest arm fall.
The arms are soft in Melee and Ultimate but hard in Brawl.
which can display the battle itself, a symbol representing the upcoming variation during a stage transition

Many players will choose to "wait out" the Fire and Rock transformations by moving to the opposite side of the stage as their opponent, without approaching or attacking them, until the transformation returns to neutral.
As a result, many players complain that the transformations result in several minutes of wasted time during a set.
On the fire variant, if a character gets hit towards the right side of the tree's base, there's a chance they will fall through.
